final_prompt:
I want a habit tracker app built in the current directory, /private/tmp/pgbench/cwd-guided, which is empty and not a git repository. I'm not sure yet about platform, stack, or feature set, so settle those with me before writing any code, because a wrong stack choice means rework.

Step 1: Interview me with the AskUserQuestion tool. Cover platform (web, mobile, desktop or CLI), preferred language and framework, where data lives (local only, or a backend and accounts), core features (daily check-ins, streaks, reminders, stats or charts), and whether I want a minimal first version. Ask only what you can't reasonably decide yourself, and offer a recommended default with each question.

Step 2: Write the agreed scope to SPEC.md. Include the stack, the features in the first version, and what is explicitly left out. Stop and wait for my approval of the spec before editing anything else.

Step 3: After I approve, build the first version exactly as specced. Add no features, abstractions, or dependencies beyond the spec. Report anything extra you think is worth adding instead of building it. Make small, targeted files rather than one large one.

Step 4: Verify real behaviour, not only unit tests. Add tests for the streak and completion logic. Then run the app and exercise the main flow: create a habit, mark it done across more than one day, and confirm the streak and stats update. Show me the commands you ran and their output. If something fails, fix the root cause rather than weakening the test.

Post a one-line note before you start each step and a short recap at the end. Local, reversible work can proceed without asking. Confirm with me before installing global tools, deleting files, or doing anything outside this directory.

You're done when the spec is approved, the app runs, the tests pass, and you have shown me the main flow working, with a short README section on how to run it.
